title: New workbooks and sheets
summary: openpyxl.Workbook() makes a new workbook with one sheet. Rename sheets with .title, add rows with ws.append([...]), add sheets with wb.create_sheet("Name"), and save.
objectives: Create a new workbook and rename its first sheet.
Build a summary sheet from data in another workbook.

slides.h: By the end: a report file made from scratch
slides.say: Every month Meera makes a fresh “low stock” file for the buyer. By the end of this lesson Python makes it: a new workbook, a header row and one row per item.
points: It starts with one sheet, `wb.active`, called “Sheet”.
p: Every month Meera makes a fresh “low stock” file for the buyer. By the end of this lesson Python makes it: a new workbook, a header row and one row per item.
It starts with one sheet, `wb.active`, called “Sheet”.

visual.text:
import openpyxl
wb = openpyxl.Workbook()
ws = wb.active
ws.title = "Low stock"
ws.append(["Item", "Qty"])
ws.append(["Erasers", 0])
ws.append(["Rulers", 45])
wb.save("low_stock.xlsx")
notes: append adds a whole row under the last one

slides.say: `ws.append(list)` writes the list into the next empty row, one value per column. It’s the easiest way to build a table.
points: The first append goes in row 1, the next in row 2…
Give it a list (or tuple) of values.

slides.h: Copying what you need into a new file
slides.say: A common job: read one workbook, write a smaller one. Two workbooks, two names: keep `src` and `out` clear.
p: A common job: read one workbook, write a smaller one. Two workbooks, two names: keep `src` and `out` clear.

visual.text:
import openpyxl
wb = openpyxl.load_workbook("stock.xlsx")
ws = wb["Stock"]
out = openpyxl.Workbook()
low = out.active
low.title = "Low stock"
low.append(["Item", "Qty"])
for item, qty, price in ws.iter_rows(min_row=2, values_only=True):
    if qty < 50:
        low.append([item, qty])
out.save("low_stock.xlsx")

tasks.model:
import openpyxl
wb = openpyxl.load_workbook("stock.xlsx")
ws = wb["Stock"]
out = openpyxl.Workbook()
low = out.active
low.title = "Low stock"
low.append(["Item", "Qty"])
none = out.create_sheet("Out of stock")
none.append(["Item"])
for item, qty, price in ws.iter_rows(min_row=2, values_only=True):
    if qty < 50:
        low.append([item, qty])
    if qty == 0:
        none.append([item])
out.save("low_stock.xlsx")

tasks.prompt: From **marks.xlsx** (sheet **Marks**), make **pass_list.xlsx** with a sheet **Passed** listing the **Name** and **Maths** mark of everyone with 40 or more in Maths, under a header **Name, Maths**. Print **N passed**.
tasks.model:
import openpyxl
ws = openpyxl.load_workbook("marks.xlsx")["Marks"]
out = openpyxl.Workbook()
p = out.active
p.title = "Passed"
p.append(["Name", "Maths"])
n = 0
for name, maths, science, english in ws.iter_rows(min_row=2, values_only=True):
    if maths >= 40:
        p.append([name, maths])
        n += 1
out.save("pass_list.xlsx")
print(f"{n} passed")

practice.prompt: Make **times.xlsx** with a sheet **Table** holding the 7 times table: column A is 1 to 10, column B is 7 × that number. No header.
practice.model:
import openpyxl
wb = openpyxl.Workbook()
ws = wb.active
ws.title = "Table"
for i in range(1, 11):
    ws.append([i, 7 * i])
